audits.title: Audit on Decisions Relating to Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) in 2 Older Adult Inpatient Wards
audits.standard: National standards for discussion and documentation of DNACPR decisions
audits.setting: Two older adult psychiatric inpatient wards, Thurrock Community Hospital

cycle1.result: 13/38 (34.21%) had a DNACPR form, 10/13 (76.92%) complete; no CPR discussion in 29/38 (76.32%); mental capacity assessments and best interest meetings documented in 0% of the 4 patients without LPA.

audits.citation: Philip J, Cherian V, Ford J. Audit on Decisions Relating to Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) in 2 Older Adult Inpatient Wards. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S255-S255. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.617.

audits.title: To resuscitate or not to resuscitate; a question for old age psychiatrists
audits.standard: Current standards for frequency and quality of resuscitation decision documentation (not specified)
audits.setting: Older adult psychiatric acute wards, North East London NHS Foundation Trust (Goodmayes Hospital)

cycle1.result: Resuscitation decisions made for 4% of patients

audits.intervention: Changes implemented after the initial audit; details not reported

cycle2.result: Resuscitation decisions made for 40% (n = 10); DNACPR orders adequately completed in each case; standard for recording decisions on the electronic record not met

audits.other_findings: Most DNACPR decisions (n = 8) were in dementia and clinicians more often considered decisions in organic than functional disorders; patient, family or carer was involved in every decision.
audits.citation: Embliss L, Bhat M. To resuscitate or not to resuscitate; a question for old age psychiatrists. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S21-S22.

audits.title: Audit of resuscitation decisions has little impact on clinical practice.
audits.setting: Medical and elderly patients, The Whittington Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Recording of resuscitation decisions 50% before the audit cycle.

audits.intervention: Clinical audit feedback and a resuscitation proforma.

cycle2.result: Recording rose to 73% (p = 0.02) over a two-month audit cycle but was not maintained.

audits.other_findings: Neither discussion with patients nor consultant involvement improved over nine years.
audits.citation: Hayes S, Henshaw D, Rai GS, Stewart K. Audit of resuscitation decisions has little impact on clinical practice. J R Coll Physicians Lond. 1999;33(4):348-350. PMID: 10472023.

audits.title: Clinical audit on documentation of anticipatory "not for resuscitation" orders in a tertiary Australian teaching hospital.

cycle1.result: Prognosis documented in 40%; palliative care offered to two-thirds with NFR; CPR process and outcomes mostly undocumented; under 50% showed the NFR reason matched patient choices.

audits.citation: Salins NS, Jansen W. Clinical audit on documentation of anticipatory "not for resuscitation" orders in a tertiary Australian teaching hospital. Indian J Palliat Care. 2011;17(1):42-46. doi:10.4103/0973-1075.78448. PMID: 21633620.

audits.title: General Surgery Resuscitation Preference Documentation: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.standard: Aim to increase documented resuscitation status from 82% to 90% within 1 year
audits.setting: Large tertiary care centre, general surgery
audits.intervention: Consent forms modified to include resuscitation status, status added to perioperative surgical checklist, updated patient resources
audits.other_findings: High uptake of new consent forms, moderate use of checklist.
audits.citation: Jin HJ, Koichopolos J, Moffat B, Colquhoun P, Morgan B, Elliot L, et al.. General Surgery Resuscitation Preference Documentation: A Quality Improvement Initiative. J Healthc Qual. 2024;46(3):188-195. doi:10.1097/jhq.0000000000000439. PMID: 38697096.

audits.title: DNA CPR SCOTLAND POLICY: AN AUDIT OF THE SUCCESS OF IMPLEMENTATION IN NHS TAYSIDE
audits.standard: Scottish Government National DNACPR Integrated Adult Policy (2010)
audits.setting: NHS Tayside: oncology, cardiology, medicine for the elderly and Cornhill Macmillan Centre (hospice)

cycle1.result: DNACPR form present or completed during admission: Cornhill 92% (25/27), oncology 78% (23/30), cardiology 19% (10/52), MFE 29% (7/24); form went with patient on discharge/transfer in 100% Cornhill, 4% oncology, none cardiology or MFE.

audits.other_findings: On admission forms present in 18% (5/27) Cornhill and 23% (7/30) oncology, none in cardiology or MFE; many without forms had metastatic cancer or poor performance status.
audits.citation: Douglas C, Harrison M, Todd A, Munro J, Essex J, Karuny B. DNA CPR SCOTLAND POLICY: AN AUDIT OF THE SUCCESS OF IMPLEMENTATION IN NHS TAYSIDE. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2014;4(Suppl 1):A110.2-A110. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2014-000654.317.
